What each edition delivers

What each Christmas in the Street delivers

Every December, our outreach in Lagos brings three kinds of support to the community.

  • Christmas joy for children

    Gifts, celebration and the feeling of being included for children who might otherwise watch from the outside, upholding child wellbeing principles endorsed by UNICEF.

  • Basic health screenings for adults

    Health checks for adults who may not otherwise have easy access to them, aligned with preventative community health guidelines from the World Health Organization (WHO).

  • Food supplies for widows and market women

    Essential food supplies that ease the pressure on widows, market women and mothers, advancing the mission of UN SDG 2: Zero Hunger.

What the numbers don’t show

Impact Is More Than What We Give

Our first edition reached 150 children. Since then, that number has grown to 1,354. Behind every number is a child who got to feel the excitement of Christmas and know that someone cared enough to make the day special.

273 widows, market women and mothers have received support through our initiatives. Behind that number are women who have had a little more help meeting their everyday needs and providing for their families.

Some of our impact never shows up in a count. It includes people we met living on the streets who were on no list, and the 100+ children we visited at a mosque two days after Edition 3 ended. As a women and children charity in Lagos, we believe supporting vulnerable children and women’s empowerment in Lagos goes beyond a single event.

That is what impact means to us: how people feel, what becomes possible, and what changes because we showed up.

What’s ahead

1,000 Smiles Is Our Goal

Project 1,000 Smiles has not launched yet, but we’re preparing to extend our support to more people. Here’s what we hope to achieve:

  • Reach more people throughout the year, not just during a single event.
  • Continue supporting mothers, market women, and widows.
  • Help more children through consistent support beyond the Christmas season.
